newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products steady to firm.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products steady to firm.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were steady to firm on Thursday, traders said.

Naphtha trod water for much of the day following heavy buffeting by recent crude volatility. Shipping difficulties were a major problem. "All I can think about is getting a ship even if freight is telephone numbers," said one refiner with two cargoes coming available in the second half. Cif Med naptha was pegged in the low $220s.

Gasoline demand was seen in the east Med for combi cargoes, but again high freight costs of up to $20 a tonne, have hampered trading opportunities. There was some talk of an arb opportunity to the Gulf opening following the closure of the t/a arb.
High sulphur fuel oil recovered to the end of the day after falling below $100 a tonne fob Med on swaps markets, amid talk of fresh Venezuelan material moving into the region, traders said.

Ship brokers said the 85,000 tonne Omegaventure L, the 85,000 tonne Progress and the 52,000 tonne Alkman had all been fixed over the past few days from Venezuela or the US Gulf with UKCont and Med options. Some was expected to cover demand into Romania, while the rest is expected to move to ARA.

Low sulphur fuel oil was stable, with swaps pegged at around $109/$110 fob NWE. A little fresh buying interest is seen emerging, with one trader saying he may be prepared to pay around the mean of fob NWE quotes. But Italian demand does not appear to have stirred.
Gas oil gained $5.25 a tonne on a stronger screen following forecasts of colder weather in the northeastern United States.

Trade continued very thin, hampered by lack of vessels. Non-Russian 0.2 percent heating oil was well offered but few buyers emerged. Russian heating oil cargoes were again notionally assessed at well over high cif quotes +$3 but high freight rates cast a pall over the market
Black Sea to Mediterranean is seen over 250 WSC. "It's a real question whether there are real buyers out there, a trader said."
